bib.title: JARVIS-1: Open-world Multi-task Agents with Memory-Augmented Multimodal Language Models

question: How can an open-world Minecraft agent plan over long horizons from multimodal input and keep improving across tasks without gradient updates?
hypothesis: A multimodal LM planner with interactive self-check/self-explain and a multimodal experience memory (retrieved in context) will plan more correctly and improve with accumulated experience, especially on long-horizon tasks.
contributions: From LLMs to MLMs: chain MineCLIP with an LLM so planning is situation-aware and uses multimodal feedback for self-check and self-explain.
Multimodal memory: store successful plans keyed by task and observation and retrieve them as in-context references, with no model update.
Self-instruct and self-improve: the agent proposes its own tasks, with distributed agents filling a shared memory.

method.summary: JARVIS-1 chains MineCLIP and GPT into a multimodal language model that writes code-like plans of short-horizon goals from task, text-ized observation and inventory. Plans are checked by simulated execution (self-check), repaired from failure feedback (self-explain), and conditioned on top-k retrieved past successful plans from a key-value multimodal memory. A goal-conditioned controller (STEVE-1 for mine goals, direct craft/smelt actions) executes the goals; memory is filled by GPT-generated self-instruct curricula run in distributed environments.
method.task: open-world instruction following in Minecraft 1.16.5 survival mode (200+ tasks, Minecraft Universe Benchmark)

datasets.name: Minecraft Universe Benchmark (MCU) task subset
datasets.size: over 200 tasks in 11 groups (Wood 34, Wood-Variants 43, Stone 10, Iron 22, Gold 9, Diamond 7, Redstone 7, Blocks 15, Armor 17, Decoration 17, Food 9)
datasets.split: at least 30 tests per task with different seeds

datasets.name: Minecraft text data from the internet
datasets.size: inferred: approximately 1000 Minecraft text entries (Appendix A.2); also 'a substantial amount' used to fine-tune LLaMA2 13B, size not given
datasets.preprocessing: keywords of Minecraft items extracted from the wiki; GPT generates descriptive sentences; similarity to current MineCLIP visual observation selects text for the prompt

models.name: JARVIS-1 planner (MLM: GPT + MineCLIP)
models.architecture: language part from GPT (OpenAI, 2023, ChatGPT/GPT-4), vision from MineCLIP; everything converted to language

models.name: STEVE-1 controller
models.architecture: goal-conditioned policy built on VPT with MineCLIP text conditioning

models.name: GPT, ReAct, Inner Monologue, DEPS
models.architecture: LLM planners reproduced for Minecraft via prompt and feedback templates, accessed through OpenAI API

inference.temperature: all LLM hyper-parameters including temperature kept at API default (value not stated)
inference.samples: at least 30 tests per task with different seeds, average success rate (main); at least 20 seeds on task subset for LM ablation; 300+ seeds for ObtainDiamondPickaxe curve; diamond_pickaxe in Table 9 evaluated 692 times
inference.prompting: few-shot, code-style plan (mine/craft calls with step comments) using one in-context example plus retrieved memory plans; separate prompts for planning, goal parsing, self-explain, self-check
inference.retrieval: key-value memory (keys: task + visual state; values: successfully executed plans). Query generation by LLM backward reasoning to sub-tasks with bounded depth; CLIP text encoder similarity above a confidence threshold selects candidates, then ranked by CLIP visual similarity of states; top entry per sub-goal retrieved. Threshold value and k not stated.

parameters.memory_epochs: 4 epochs of interaction with all task sets before evaluation
parameters.controller: STEVE-1 for mine goals; craft and smelt executed directly by environment

other.environment_rules: Minecraft 1.16.5 survival; peaceful difficulty, doDaylightCycle false, keepInventory true, night_vision effect
other.max_steps: 12k, 36k or 12-36k per group; 72000 steps (60 min) for the long-horizon run; 24,000 steps = 20 minutes

metrics.name: success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of episodes where target object obtained within max steps, start in survival with empty inventory unless stated; averaged over at least 30 seeds; group mean and variance reported

eval.protocol: no demonstrations; success rate averaged over seeds; variance across tasks per group given as +/-; no significance test

availability.code: project page craftjarvis.org/JARVIS-1 (no repo URL stated in text)

evidence.quote: all hyper-parameters of LLM including temperature are kept as default.

results.claim: JARVIS-1 averages 8.99% on the Diamond group versus 2.42% for DEPS, the strongest baseline.
results.setup: Minecraft Diamond group (7 tasks), 36k max steps, iron_axe initial inventory, memory filled by 4 epochs of self-instruct
results.quote: the success rate has increased by nearly 3 times (8.99% vs 2.42%)
results.note: the ratio 8.99/2.42 is about 3.7x, text says nearly 3 times; Fig 2 shows 3.39x for a different comparison

results.claim: On ObtainDiamondPickaxe within 20 minutes JARVIS-1 reaches 6.22% versus 2.5% for RL-finetuned VPT.
results.setup: ObtainDiamondPickaxe, 20 min gameplay, empty inventory, 4 epochs of memory; VPT figure from Baker et al.
results.note: printed as 6.2% and 6% elsewhere (Sec 4.3, Fig 1); Table 9 lists 0.0622 over 692 evals

results.claim: Extending gameplay to 60 minutes (72000 steps) doubles diamond pickaxe success to 12.5%, while VPT barely changes (2.5% to 3%).
results.quote: JARVIS-1’s success rate in acquiring a diamond pickaxe improved from 6.2% to 12.5%.

results.claim: JARVIS-1 beats all baselines in every task group; on Iron it gets 34.63 against DEPS 16.92.
results.table: Table 2, row Iron AVG, columns JARVIS-1 (34.63±10.61) and DEPS (16.92±4.69)

results.claim: On the Wood group JARVIS-1 averages 88.84% versus GPT 27.30%.
results.table: Table 2, row Wood AVG, columns JARVIS-1 and GPT

results.claim: JARVIS-1 needs 2-3 re-planning rounds to get a correct executable plan versus more than 6 for DEPS.
results.setup: Minecraft tasks, JARVIS-1 with memory vs DEPS
results.quote: JARVIS-1 usually only requires 2-3 rounds of re-planning to generate the correct executable plan, whereas
results.note: no table or per-task data; the sentence continues 'DEPS requires more than 6 rounds'

results.claim: After 4 epochs of learning the memory held 425 successful trajectories, and success rose with memory size for all key items.
results.setup: JARVIS-1 self-improvement over 4 epochs on all tasks
results.quote: After 4 epochs of learning, JARVIS-1 had accumulated a total of 425 successful trajectories in its memory.

results.claim: ChatGPT with memory reaches nearly the same success as GPT-4; pre-trained LLaMA2-70B is far worse and fine-tuned LLaMA2-13B on Minecraft text is close to ChatGPT.
results.setup: Subset of tasks (crafting table to diamond), 4 epochs of memory learning; bar values only in Fig 6, not recoverable from text order

results.claim: Reasoning before retrieval and multimodal retrieval improve results over text-only retrieval (best: multimodal memory + reasoning).
results.setup: Subset of tasks: stone pickaxe, iron pickaxe, shield, diamond, redstone block; bar values in Fig 8
results.quote: reasoning before retrieval can effectively improve retrieval accuracy

results.claim: A GPT-generated self-instruct curriculum gives the best 60-minute diamond pickaxe result versus human-written and random curricula.
results.setup: three JARVIS-1 variants, 4 epochs of curriculum experience, 60 min
results.quote: JARVIS-1 with a GPT-generated curriculum can finish the task within the shortest game-playing steps and achieve the best performance in 60 minutes

limits: Bottleneck on diamond tasks is the controller's imperfect execution of short-horizon text goals, not the planner (Sec 4.2).
Absolute success on long-horizon groups stays low (Gold 6.85, Diamond 8.99, Armor 13.44).
Baselines (GPT, ReAct, Inner Monologue, DEPS) are reproduced by the authors, not the original implementations.
Memory stores only successful trajectories; threshold, k, query-depth and other retrieval settings are not given.
Peaceful mode, permanent daytime, keepInventory and night vision make the environment easier than standard survival.
Human comparison covers only 10 minutes of gameplay due to resource constraints.
No code repository, weights or compute figures stated; LLM temperature left at API default and API models can change.
Memory ablations and LM comparison reported as figures only, on task subsets.

terms.definition: a key-value memory where the keys are multimodal, comprising both the task and the observation (or situation) made when this memory entry was created. The values are the plans that were successfully executed.
ask JARVIS-1 to progressively simulate the plan execution, predict the resulting state after each step (primarily the state of inventory), and evaluate them
explain the error and locate the bugs in the original plan from environment feedback, then re-plan
improving planning by retrieving stored experiences into the prompt, with no gradient update

lineage.note: interactive planning with self-explain; main baseline, JARVIS-1 adds memory and multimodal input
